files.purpose: Draws a Hydra head's progress as a single 28pt-tall Canvas of 3pt staves, one stave per tool call or assistant reply in timeline order, whose height encodes how much the step changed (lookup 0.45, command 0.65, edit 0.85, reply 1.0) and whose colour is the head's persona tint at varying opacity; a count line ('3 edits · 2 commands · 5 reads') sits under it and hovering a stave shows a 260pt glass card naming that step. The file also holds the compact 'Show what heads are doing' off-mode panel (HydraHeadProgress) that centres the head's task title over the bar, the breathing/sweeping task title (HydraWorkingTitle), the per-second elapsed-time label (HydraElapsedTime), the hover card surface modifier and a global SweepBudget that caps the highlight sweep animation to 3 running bars at once for performance.

side_effects: Mutates the global SweepBudget.shared: .task(id: isRunning) joins with ObjectIdentifier(runtime) when running, leaves when not running; .onDisappear leaves.

Two sleeping tasks: .task(id: isRunning ? -1 : events.count) sets isSettled=false, and when not running sleeps rise+0.1 = 0.55 s then sets isSettled=true; .task(id: events.count) (skipped if events empty or reduce motion) sets isRising=true, sleeps 0.55 s, sets isRising=false. Cancelled sleeps return early without flipping state.
No persistence, no I/O, no network.

ui_elements: Bar: Canvas height 28pt; staves 3pt wide, 3pt gap, pitch 6pt; each stave a rounded rect with cornerRadius 1.5 (staveWidth/2) filled from the baseline up.
Capacity = max(1, floor((width + 3) / 6)); when there are more events than capacity only the latest `capacity` staves are drawn (oldest slide off the left).
Stave height share: lookup 0.45, command 0.65, edit 0.85, reply 1.0 of bar height.
Stave colours: edit and reply = tint; command = tint.opacity(0.7); lookup = tint.opacity(0.4). Fill order lookup, command, edit, reply (one path per kind).
Last stave override: status .failed -> Chrome.danger; status .stopped -> Chrome.secondaryText.
Hovered stave: extra fill .white.opacity(0.4) over it.
Empty slots (staves.count..<capacity): rounded rects 0.45 of bar height, cornerSize 1.5x1.5, filled Chrome.overlay(0.06).

Rise animation (lines 380-388): factor starts at 1; when rising (not reduce-motion) `let age = date.timeIntervalSince(stave.arrivedAt)` where date is the TimelineView context date and arrivedAt is `entry.item.date` (the timeline entry's own timestamp, lines 326/332), not the moment the stave first appeared on screen; if age < 0.45, `let t = max(0, age / rise)` and factor = 1 - pow(1 - t, 3) (ease-out cubic). So a bar opened on old history draws every stave at full height with no rise, and an entry dated in the future (negative age) gets t = 0 and factor 0.

Sweep highlight: band width max(24, filledWidth/3) where filledWidth = staves.count*6 - 3; cycle length 2.6 + 3.4 = 6.0 s computed from timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate; during the first 2.6 s the band x = -band + phase*(filledWidth+band); linear gradient white opacity 0 -> 0.55 -> 0, clipped to the filled staves path only.

Clock: TimelineView .animation minimumInterval 1/24 s, paused when !needsClock or ScrollActivity.shared.isScrolling; needsClock = !reduceMotion && !isSettled && (sweeps || isRising); sweeps = isRunning && !reduceMotion && SweepBudget.shared.sweeps(id).
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) holding bar then counts line.

Counts line: Text(verbatim: counts.line) font .system(.subheadline), Chrome.secondaryText, frame(maxWidth: .infinity) (centred); hidden when empty. Format parts '<n> edit'/'<n> edits', '<n> command'/'<n> commands', '<n> read'/'<n> reads' joined by ' · ' with zero parts omitted, order edits, commands, reads.
Accessibility label: '<sentence>, <elapsed>' plus ' so far' when running; sentence = parts joined by ', ' or 'Nothing done yet'.

Hover card (stepsCard): HStack spacing 8 of either MCPGlyph size 14, or Image(systemName: symbol) font .system(.callout, weight: .semibold) Chrome.secondaryText frame width 14; then Text(verbatim: step) font .system(.body, weight: .semibold) Chrome.primaryText lineLimit 1 truncation tail. Padding horizontal 12, vertical 10; frame width 260 leading; surface ProgressCardSurface; bottom padding 8 inside a zero-height frame aligned .bottom so card bottom sits 8pt above bar top; offset x = min(max(0, centre - 130), max(0, width - 260)) with centre = index*6 + 1.5; allowsHitTesting(false); transition .opacity; hover change animated .smooth(duration: 0.15).
Hover hit test: index = floor(point.x / 6) when x >= 0, y >= 0, y <= 28; only indices < staves.count are picked.
Card surface: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: Chrome.cardCornerRadius, style: .continuous); on a glass panel fill Chrome.panelControlFill(isDark:), otherwise .glassEffect(.regular).

Zero-height skip (lines 389-390): `let height = bottom * stave.height * factor; guard height > 0 else { continue }`. A stave at factor 0 (age exactly 0 or negative) is not added to `filled`, `byKind`, `ending` or `hoveredPath` for that frame, so the sweep highlight (clipped to `filled`), the failed/stopped ending colour and the hover white 0.4 fill all skip it; its slot is also not drawn as an empty slot (slots start at staves.count). The hover card overlay is independent of the canvas and still shows.

Elapsed time: inside HydraProgressBar `let elapsed = RelativeTime.duration((isRunning ? Date.now : finishedAt ?? .now).timeIntervalSince(startedAt))` (line 130) is used only in the accessibility label (line 208); the bar draws no elapsed text. The visible elapsed time is HydraElapsedTime, which the doc comment (lines 7-8) places in the strip's pill: 'how long the head has been at it sits in the strip's pill (see `HydraElapsedTime`)'. A port must not put an elapsed label under the bar.
feature_notes: Stave classification: ToolCall.kind .edit -> edit; .command -> edit if call.edits is non-empty else command; any other kind -> edit if call.edits non-empty else lookup. Assistant entries -> reply. All other entry kinds are skipped. Counts count edit/command/lookup only (reply not counted).
An MCP tool gets its MCPCatalogEntry glyph and no symbol; non-MCP tools get ToolPresentation.symbol(for: call.kind).

StaveCache hit requires equal capacity and, row-by-row, the same TimelineEntry object identity and, for tool rows, same ToolCall.status and ToolCall.title; otherwise it recomputes events, staves and counts.
The finished-bar settle task keys on -1 while running (so it does not restart per event while running) and on events.count once finished.

SweepBudget: join appends if absent; leave removes first occurrence; sweeps(id) is true when id is within the first sweepSlots (3) entries of the list; observed, so a queued bar starts sweeping when a slot frees.

HydraHeadProgress fallbacks: task = info?.task.trimmed ?? ""; status defaults .running; startedAt defaults head.createdAt; tint defaults HydraRoster.persona(at: 0).color; title falls back to head.title when task empty.

B1->B2: Only font specifications changed (fixed point sizes replaced by system text styles) plus one helper swap; line count unchanged at 603. Counts line font .system(size: 11) -> .system(.subheadline); hover card symbol .system(size: 12, weight: .semibold) -> .system(.callout, weight: .semibold); hover card step text .system(size: 13, weight: .semibold) -> .system(.body, weight: .semibold); HydraWorkingTitle .system(size: 13, weight: .medium) -> .system(.body, weight: .medium); HydraElapsedTime .system(size: 11) -> .system(.subheadline). In HydraHeadProgress `info?.task.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` became `info?.task.trimmed` (same behaviour: String.trimmed is defined in Core/Support/Text.swift as trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)). No logic, geometry or timing constants changed.

Stale comments (follow the code, not them): the doc comment at lines 14-15 says the highlight 'sweeps the filled staves every 1.8 s', but the constants are sweep: TimeInterval = 2.6 and sweepRest: TimeInterval = 3.4 (a 6.0 s cycle, line 432 `truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: sweep + sweepRest)`). The comment at lines 136-138 says the clock 'keeps going while the reader scrolls', but line 142 pauses it with `paused: !needsClock || ScrollActivity.shared.isScrolling` (the following comment at lines 140-141 matches the code).
unresolved_questions: The exact point sizes of .subheadline/.callout/.body on macOS 26 are system-defined (conventionally 11/12/13 pt, matching the B1 literals); the port should confirm against a running macOS build or ChatFont/Theme code whether any app-level scaling applies to .system(textStyle) fonts.

files.purpose: Parses the Hydra lead's aggregated heads-report message (markdown with one '## <Name>: <task> (meta)' section per head) into a HydraReportDigest holding the intro, each head's outcome, effort, landing line (files landed / did not land / changed nothing / unfinished) and report body, dropping the lead's own closing instructions from the last head. It then renders that digest as a 460pt-wide popover with a fixed header (either a stacked persona face row with totals, or a single head's name, outcome and task) above a PopoverScroll (max height 520) of per-head cards showing monospaced file rows with +/- counts and the markdown report, collapsible per head when there are several.

Two regex engines: matchFile (line 173) uses a Swift Regex literal `#/(\S+) \(\+(\d+) [−\-](\d+)\)( with conflicts)?/#` with `item.wholeMatch(of:)`, which is the Swift Regex engine, not NSRegularExpression/ICU; only the two tail patterns at line 161 (`text.range(of: suffix, options: .regularExpression)`) go through Foundation's ICU engine. In the Swift Regex default mode `\d` matches any Unicode decimal digit, but `Int(match.output.2)` / `Int(match.output.3)` (line 174) parse only ASCII digits, so an item with non-ASCII digits matches and is then dropped by the guard. A port should match ASCII-digit counts and treat anything else as a non-matching item.

Foundation String APIs: components(separatedBy:), trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces), rangeOfCharacter(from: .decimalDigits) (Unicode decimal digits, not just ASCII), replacingOccurrences, range(of:options: .backwards).

(.subheadline, secondaryText); blocks ready -> eager VStack(spacing 8) of MarkdownBlockView per block, padding top 2, font .system(.callout), markdownPointSize 12, markdownDimmed false, text selection enabled; blocks pending -> ProgressView small with vertical padding 8.
feature_notes: parse: splits on "\n"; a line whose whitespace-trimmed form starts with '## ' and whose text before the first ':' (trimmed) is a HydraRoster name starts a head section; lines before the first section form the intro (joined, trimmed; nil when empty). Other '## ' headings stay in the body.

Per section: leading blank lines skipped; if the first remaining line starts (after whitespace trim) with 'Landed in your checkout:', 'Did not land', 'Changed nothing.' or 'Nothing landed', it is parsed as the landing line and removed; the rest joined and trimmed is the body; the LAST section's body passes through withoutLeadInstructions. Head id = name.

parseHeader (lines 88-119): name is text before the first colon, rest after it (both space-trimmed). Its no-colon branch (`name = trimmed; rest = ""`, lines 95-97) is unreachable: parseHeader is called only from parse (line 61), on section headers that passed isHeadHeader, which returns false without a colon (`guard let colon = header.firstIndex(of: ":") else { return false }`, line 81). While rest ends with ')' and contains '(', the last '(...)' group is meta if lowercased == 'failed', lowercased hasPrefix 'stopped', it contains any decimal digit (`rangeOfCharacter(from: .decimalDigits)`), or it is one of {low, medium, high, xhigh, max, minimal, fast, default}; meta groups are stripped; 'failed' -> .failed; 'stopped...' -> .stopped; otherwise a non-empty group is an effort with ', ' replaced by ' · ', inserted at the front. Efforts are joined by ' · '. The first non-meta group stops the loop.

parseLanding: 'Changed nothing.' -> .nothing; 'Nothing landed' -> .unfinished with path after 'in its copy at ' (trimmed, trailing '.' dropped, empty -> nil) or nil; 'Landed in your checkout:' -> .landed(parseFiles(rest)); 'Did not land' -> optional ' (<error>)' captured up to the first ')' and whitespace-trimmed, optional ':' dropped, .notLanded(files, error or nil when empty); otherwise .none.

parseFiles (lines 157-169): trim, drop one trailing '.', remove regex tails in order '; \d+ build-output files? (was|were) left out$' then ', and \d+ more$', split on ', ' (`text.components(separatedBy: ", ")`), trim spaces of each item, keep items that wholly match '(\S+) \(\+(\d+) [−\-](\d+)\)( with conflicts)?' (U+2212 minus or ASCII hyphen). Non-matching items are silently dropped. Consequence: a path containing a space (for example 'My Project/x.ts (+1 −2)') can never match because `\S+` must be the whole path under wholeMatch, and a path containing ', ' is cut into pieces by the split; either way that file vanishes from the card's file rows, from filesLine and from totalsLine (both count only parsed files). On Windows, paths with spaces are common, so this is a real parity hazard to reproduce or flag.

leadPrefixes (verbatim): 'The changes listed above', 'The heads worked in your checkout', 'A file listed with conflicts', 'Do not check any of this', 'Do not wait for', 'A head that failed', 'A head the user stopped', 'The user queued', 'The user sent'. withoutLeadInstructions removes the last '\n\n'-separated paragraph when it starts with one of these, then trims.

cleanedTitle: for each non-empty name, while the string starts with '<name>: ' or '<name> ' AND what follows that prefix again starts with one of those prefixes, drop the first prefix (so 'Juno: Juno: x' -> 'Juno: x'; a single prefix is kept). withoutNamePrefix drops exactly one leading '<name>: ' and whitespace-trims.

stillAtWorkSentence (lines 435-445): `intro.range(of: "still at work")` is a case-sensitive, literal search ('Still at work' does not match); it backs up to just after the last '.' before the match (or the start), returns the trimmed remainder of the intro to its end, nil when empty. digest.intro is displayed nowhere else: its only uses are the two stillAtWorkSentence calls in the multi-head header (line 303) and the single-head header (line 344), so an intro without 'still at work' is never shown and the text before that sentence is never shown.

persona(for:): first the passed personas matched by name, then HydraRoster.persona(named:), else HydraRoster.persona(at: 0). status mapping: done -> .completed, failed -> .failed, stopped -> .stopped.
hasReport is false when the body is empty or exactly 'No report.'.

B1->B2: file shrank from 662 to 655 lines. (1) All `trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)` calls in parse, parseLanding, parseFiles, withoutLeadInstructions and stillAtWorkSentence became `.trimmed` (same semantics; stillAtWorkSentence now wraps the substring in String(...) first). (2) The static NSRegularExpression `filePattern` (pattern ^(\S+) \(\+(\d+) [−\-](\d+)\)( with conflicts)?$ built with try!) was removed and matchFile now uses a Swift Regex literal with item.wholeMatch(of:) and match.output.1-4; the accepted grammar is the same. (3) The body's `.environment(\.chatZoom, 1)` with the comment 'The popover reads at its own size, not the conversation's zoom.' was removed (the chatZoom environment key no longer exists anywhere in B2). (4) Fonts moved from fixed sizes to text styles: size 11 -> .subheadline (overflow count, totals, still-at-work, outcome caption, files line, Failed/Stopped, effort, Did not land, Changed nothing., Nothing landed, No report.), size 11 monospaced -> .subheadline monospaced (copy path, file rows), size 13 semibold -> .body semibold (title, head names), size 12 -> .callout (task lines, report body), chevron size 10 semibold -> .footnote semibold. The report body's .environment(\.markdownPointSize, 12) is unchanged.

Duplicate names: Head.id = name (line 73 `Head(id: name, name: name, ...)`), the cards' ForEach is keyed `id: \.element.id` (line 244), and `expanded` (lines 473-477) and `blocks` (lines 230, 256, 262, 635) are keyed by head.name. Two sections with the same roster name therefore share one expand toggle and one blocks entry (in the warm pass the later head's parsed body overwrites the earlier one, so both cards show the later report when expanded), and the ForEach gets duplicate ids.

Zero heads: when parse finds no roster header, `single` (line 212, `digest.heads.count == 1 ? digest.heads.first : nil`) is nil and `collapsible` (line 241, `digest.heads.count > 1`) is false, so the multi-head header still renders with the persona faces, the cleaned title and totalsLine '0 heads' (line 425 `"\(n) \(n == 1 ? "head" : "heads")"`), above a Divider and an empty PopoverScroll (padding 0); the .task returns at once because `missing` is empty.

Two sources: the header's faces and '+N' overflow come from the `personas` init argument (line 279 `ForEach(Array(personas.prefix(9)), id: \.self)`, line 285 `personas.count - 9`), and the multi-head title is `cleanedTitle(title, names: personas.map(\.name))` (line 295), while the totals line counts `digest.heads` (line 416). The face count and the '<n> heads' count can therefore disagree. persona(for:) also prefers the `personas` list by name before HydraRoster.

files.purpose: Computes, from recorded TurnRecord token spends and each head's HydraHeadInfo phase timestamps, a conversation-scoped HydraRunMetrics snapshot: lead and heads token totals (nil when nothing recorded, never shown as zero), per provider/model groups sorted biggest first, and per-head queue/startup/run/landing phases. It renders that snapshot as an equatable flat card under the Hydra panel strip with a headline, Lead/Heads/Total rows, group rows, head timings and explanatory notes, while a .task makes sure the lead and head runtimes' histories are loaded.
key_symbols: struct HydraRunMetrics: Equatable { var lead = Scope(); var heads = Scope(); var timings: [HeadTiming] = []; var recordedTokens: Int?; var isPartial: Bool; var spansProviders: Bool; var hasTimings: Bool }

HydraRunMetrics.Scope: Equatable { var turns = 0; var turnsWithUsage = 0; var hasUnloadedHistory = false; var tokens: Int?; var groups: [Group] = []; var isPartial: Bool { hasUnloadedHistory || (tokens == nil ? turns > 0 : turnsWithUsage < turns) } }
HydraRunMetrics.Group: Equatable, Identifiable { var id: String; var provider: ProviderKind; var model: String?; var tokens: Int }
enum HydraRunMetrics.Phase: Equatable { case measured(TimeInterval); case running; case unavailable; var text: String }

HydraRunMetrics.HeadTiming: Equatable, Identifiable { var id: UUID; var personaIndex: Int; var name: String; var status: HydraHeadInfo.Status; var queue: Phase = .unavailable; var startup: Phase = .unavailable; var execution: Phase = .unavailable; var landing: Phase? }

@MainActor enum HydraRunMetricsReader { static func snapshot(leadTurns: [TurnRecord], heads: [ChatThread], headTurns: @MainActor (ChatThread) -> [TurnRecord]?) -> HydraRunMetrics; private static func spend(in:) -> Scope; private static func merged(_:) -> [Group]; private static func timing(of:) -> HeadTiming?; private static func phase(from:to:isRunning:) -> Phase }
struct HydraRunMetricsView: View { @Environment(AppModel.self) model; let runtime: ThreadRuntime; let heads: [ChatThread]; private var snapshot: HydraRunMetrics }

private struct HydraRunMetricsCard: View, Equatable { @Environment(AppModel.self) model; @Environment(\.colorScheme); let metrics: HydraRunMetrics; static func == compares metrics only; headline; totalText; scopeRow(_:_:); scopeText(_:); groupRow(_:scope:); modelName(_:); timingRow(_:); phaseText(_:); notes; note(_:) }
calls_into: TurnRecord.tokenSpends (entries with provider: ProviderKind, model: String?, totalTokens: Int)
ChatThread.hydra (HydraHeadInfo: index, persona.name, status, queuedAt, startedAt, executionStartedAt, executionFinishedAt, landingStartedAt, landingFinishedAt), ChatThread.id
state_owned: No @State. The snapshot is recomputed from runtime.turns and each loaded head runtime's turns every time HydraRunMetricsView.body evaluates; the card is .equatable() so it redraws only when the snapshot differs.
side_effects: .task(id: heads.map(\.id)): awaits runtime.ensureLoaded(), then for each head (stopping if cancelled) awaits model.runtime(for: head.id).ensureLoaded(); model.runtime(for:) may create a runtime for the head. Loading history is the only side effect.

System text styles .callout and .subheadline plus literal sizes 12.5 and 10.5; .monospacedDigit() on Font.

Headline VStack(spacing 2): 'No usage recorded yet' when recordedTokens is nil, else 'Recorded usage and timings', font .system(size: 12.5, weight: .semibold) primaryText; subtitle 'This conversation's lead and heads, as their turns reported it' font .system(.subheadline) secondaryText, fixedSize vertical.

Model name = provider model shortName, else raw model id, else provider displayName.

Timings (when any): Divider, 'Head timings' (.system(.callout, weight: .medium) primaryText), then per head VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 3): HStack(spacing 6) of `HydraGlyph(persona: HydraRoster.persona(at: timing.personaIndex), size: 14, isRunning: timing.status == .running, status: timing.status)` (line 348; personaIndex comes from info.index, while the name comes from info.persona.name, lines 170-171), name Text(verbatim: timing.name) (.system(.callout) primaryText lineLimit 1), MiniSpinner when running, Spacer(minLength: 8); then phase text (.system(.subheadline).monospacedDigit() secondaryText, fixedSize vertical, leading padding 20). Each row has `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` and `.accessibilityLabel(Text("\(timing.name), \(phaseText(timing))"))` (lines 362-363). Phase text: 'Queue <x> · Startup <x> · Run <x>' plus ' · Landing <x>' when a landing phase exists; <x> is RelativeTime.duration(max(0, s)), 'in progress' or 'unavailable'.

Notes VStack(spacing 3), font .system(size: 10.5) secondaryText fixedSize vertical: always 'Totals cover the conversation and its retained heads, not one run. Providers may omit usage for some requests.'; when partial 'Some turns recorded no usage, so the totals are lower bounds.'; when more than one provider 'Recorded across providers, so the total guides rather than bills.'; when timings exist 'Heads work at the same time, so their durations overlap and are not added up.'
feature_notes: spend(in:): turns = count; a turn counts toward turnsWithUsage only if tokenSpends is non-nil and non-empty; each spend adds totalTokens to the total and to the group keyed '<provider.rawValue>|<model ?? "">'; tokens stays nil when no turn had usage.

snapshot (lines 93-125): for each head, `if let timing = timing(of: head) { timings.append(timing) }` runs before `guard let turns = headTurns(head) else { headScope.hasUnloadedHistory = true; continue }`, so a head whose history is not loaded (runtime missing or isLoadingHistory) still gets its timing row while contributing no turns and setting heads.hasUnloadedHistory = true; head tokens sum only when a head recorded some. Groups are merged by id and sorted by tokens descending, ties by id ascending.
recordedTokens is the sum of lead and heads tokens, either alone, or nil when both nil. spansProviders is true when the union of lead and heads groups has more than one distinct ProviderKind.

timing(of:): nil when head.hydra is nil; queue = startedAt - queuedAt when queuedAt exists; startup = executionStartedAt - startedAt when executionStartedAt exists; execution = phase(executionStartedAt, executionFinishedAt); landing is set only when landingStartedAt or landingFinishedAt exists. phase(): no start -> unavailable; no end -> running if status == .running else unavailable; else measured(end - start).

B1->B2: Only font changes (line count unchanged at 398): 'Total recorded' and its value size 12 medium -> .callout medium; 'Head timings' size 12 medium -> .callout medium; headline subtitle size 11 -> .subheadline; scope row label and value size 12 -> .callout; group row model and tokens size 11 -> .subheadline; timing name size 12 -> .callout; phase text size 11 -> .subheadline. The headline's .system(size: 12.5, weight: .semibold) and the notes' .system(size: 10.5) remain fixed sizes. No logic change.
unresolved_questions: UsagePanel.tokens formatting, RelativeTime.duration formatting and MiniSpinner visuals are defined in other files.
Where HydraRunMetricsView is mounted (panel strip) and how it is opened are outside this file.

files.purpose: Renders a usage-limit notice as a timeline pill for a thread that is auto-continuing after hitting a provider usage limit: an info icon and the notice text, plus 'Cancel' and 'New thread' plain buttons while the wait is live. Once the wait is over it replaces the notice message with a past-tense outcome sentence read from the AppModel's auto-continue outcomes (cancelled, handed off or resumed).

files.purpose: The in-thread editor for a previously sent user message: it wraps PromptEditor titled 'Edit message' around the message's text and attachments, and above the actions shows a box describing what the working tree changed since that message with an optional switch to undo those file changes. Sending calls runtime.resend to rewind the thread to before the message (optionally restoring files) and resend the edit; the edit state lives on ThreadRuntime.messageEdit so closing and reopening the thread preserves it.

private enum Changes { case checking; case found(RevertPreview); case unavailable(String); init(_ result: Result<RevertPreview, Error>?) }
@State private var changes: Changes; @State private var restoresFiles = true; @State private var error: String?; @State private var isSending = false
private var canSend: Bool
@ViewBuilder private var fileChanges: some View
@ViewBuilder private func fileList(_ files: [RevertPreview.File]) -> some View
private func send(); private func cancel()

RevertPreview (files, restorable, additions, deletions) and RevertPreview.File (id, path, isKept, isBinary, additions, deletions)
state_owned: changes: Changes, initialised from runtime.cachedRevertPreview(for: edit.id) (so a preview fetched on the pencil's hover opens complete), else .checking
The edit text/attachments are owned by the PromptEdit object held on ThreadRuntime.messageEdit, not by the view.
side_effects: .task(id: edit.id) (lines 64-69) always calls `runtime.revertPreview(for: edit.id)`, awaits `.value`, and unless cancelled assigns `changes = Changes(result)`, even when init already filled `changes` from cachedRevertPreview. In ThreadRuntime (lines 1765-1789) revertPreview returns the same cached Task while the entry has the current diffRevision and is under 10 s old, and cachedRevertPreview returns a result only under that same condition, so normally the task re-assigns the same result; only if the entry expired or diffRevision changed between init and the task does a fresh preview run, and it can then replace a cached .found with a new .found or .unavailable.

send() (lines 156-171): begins `guard canSend else { return }`, so onSubmit from PromptEditor (keyboard submit) is gated exactly like the disabled Send button. Then restore = false; if changes is .found, restore = restoresFiles && !preview.files.isEmpty; sets isSending = true, error = nil, and in a Task awaits runtime.resend(edit.id, text:, attachments:, restoreFiles: restore); on success sets runtime.messageEdit = nil; on failure sets error to error.localizedDescription; always resets isSending.
cancel(): sets runtime.messageEdit = nil (closes the editor, discarding the edit).

feature_notes: canSend is false while changes is .checking (so sending cannot silently keep the files), and otherwise requires !edit.isEmpty && !isSending && !runtime.isRunning.

Send restores files only when changes is .found, restoresFiles is on and preview.files is non-empty; with .unavailable the edit is sent without restoring files.

No strings, geometry or behaviour changed.

Invisible restore: when files exist but `preview.restorable.isEmpty` (every file kept, lines 93-99) no switch is shown, yet restoresFiles keeps its default true, so send computes `restore = restoresFiles && !preview.files.isEmpty` = true (line 159) and calls resend with restoreFiles: true; there is nothing restorable, but the flag sent is true. The kept rows in that list show at opacity 0.45 because `restoresFiles && !file.isKept` is false.
